title: Strength restoration R3
summary: NH demonstrates his R3 strength restoration, built after cracking his ribs, for the intercostals, the side of the core, thoracic extension and wrist health. It pairs a hip-driven modified serratus punch with a band wrist traction, done with a very light band for 4-8 sets between heavy lifts.
claims: He built the R3 after cracking his ribs about two years earlier, since the doctor's rehab never made them feel healthy
R3 targets the ribs and thoracic area, side core strength, thoracic extension and wrist rehab; he does it every lower body day
Strength restorations should be 2-3 movements taking under a minute, supersetted between heavy movements
Modified serratus punch: band in the web between thumb and index, stand tall, rotate from the hip so the twist, not the arm, moves the band, keeping constant tension
The modified serratus punch can change your life if you have intercostal muscle pain
Band wrist traction (band around the wrist, twist, elbow pointing at the ceiling) cures wrist pain and pumps blood into poorly vascularized tendons to speed recovery
Do 4-8 sets with a very easy band; if you are sore the next day you did resistance training, not strength restoration
Injury prevention is the best way to grow because you never have to stop training
exercises: band in thumb-index web; stand straight, no leaning; rotate at the hip; arm passive; keep tension through stretch and contraction
wrap band around wrist, grab and twist, point elbow to ceiling as perpendicular as possible
wrist health, blood flow to tendons, also helps ribs
